title: Stars rain over ALMA
caption: Star trails over an ALMA antenna, Chajnantor plateau, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Stars seem to rain down on one of the 66 antennas that make up the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), on the Chajnantor Plateau high in the Chilean Andes. The downpour is really a long exposure recording the stars' trails across the sky as Earth rotates.

It is just as well this is not real rain. The plateau was chosen partly because it is so dry. Radio waves pass easily through Earth's atmosphere, but water vapour in the air soaks them up and degrades what astronomers can record.

Europe, North America and East Asia run ALMA together as an international partnership, working in cooperation with the Republic of Chile. The photo, taken by K. Ashitagawa, was provided by NAOJ, the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure star-trail photograph by K. Ashitagawa (NAOJ). The source does not publish camera or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points. The streaks appear only because the long exposure recorded Earth's rotation.
